title: PR #156 · Tab switching across the split

lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 156: Ctrl+Page Down and Up now step through both panes' tabs as one row.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one fifty-six: Control Page Down and Control Page Up now step through both panes' tabs as one row.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press Ctrl+Page Down or Up, Ctrl+Tab or Ctrl+Shift+Tab, or pick Next or Previous Tab in a tab's menu.
lines.say: You press Control Page Down or Up, Control Tab or Control Shift Tab, or pick Next or Previous Tab in a tab's menu.

lines.caption: The lookup written for issue 128 finds the tab one step over, crossing the split.
lines.say: The lookup written for issue one twenty-eight finds the tab one step over, crossing the split.

lines.caption: Past either end it finds nothing, so the new code wraps: to the left pane's first tab, or the right pane's last.
It then shows the target tab in its own pane; in the same pane, that's the whole job.
If the tab is in the other pane, the existing pane switch moves the dimming to the pane you left.
That switch activates the target tab, and its file view gets the keyboard focus.
Until now these keys cycled inside one pane; now, from bravo, the last tab on the left, they go on to charlie on the right.
Each pane is its own GTK notebook, so the code shows the target tab first, then hands over to the pane switch a click uses.
All these keys run the same two actions, which now both call one new function.
In split view, the tab after the left pane's last is the right pane's first, and the reverse going back.
The drops from issue 128 don't wrap, but tab switching always did, so it still does, over both panes.
lines.say: The drops from issue one twenty-eight don't wrap, but tab switching always did, so it still does, over both panes.

lines.caption: The target becomes its notebook's current page; within one pane, the window activates it as before.
Crossing panes, the pane switch makes the target's notebook the selected one, and the next key press starts from there.
In the test, the left pane holds alpha and bravo, and the right pane holds charlie and delta.
Next goes alpha, bravo, charlie, delta, crossing the split from bravo to charlie; previous goes back.
At the ends it wraps: from delta to alpha going forward, and from alpha to delta going back.
Without split view nothing changes: the keys cycle through the one pane's tabs, wrapping, as before.
Within a pane it switches as before; at a pane's edge it crosses over; at the very ends it wraps.
Without split view nothing changes, and the Tab keys and the tab menu's items behave the same way.
Both actions are now one line that calls the new function; the helper other actions use is unchanged.
The PR changes the window's code and adds its test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; it adds no setting and no new key.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It reuses the tab lookup from issue 128, keeps the old wrap-around, and switches panes as a click does.
lines.say: It reuses the tab lookup from issue one twenty-eight, keeps the old wrap-around, and switches panes as a click does.

lines.caption: The building session built and installed the packages in the cloud container, with no warnings in the changed files.
The test crossed from bravo to charlie and back, then wrapped from delta to alpha and back, checking each window title.
Ctrl+Tab crossed too, the focus followed into the new pane, and a window without split view still wrapped.
lines.say: Control Tab crossed too, the focus followed into the new pane, and a window without split view still wrapped.

lines.caption: The test passed in 27 seconds, the test for issue 128 passed on the first run, and all 13 screenshots passed the audit.
lines.say: The test passed in twenty-seven seconds, the test for issue one twenty-eight passed on the first run, and all thirteen screenshots passed the audit.

lines.caption: Not run: the keys with the focus on a tab label, which is only reasoned, and the tab menu's two items.
The first draft pressed Back after crossing and landed in alpha; a mouse click did the same, so it's an older quirk.
The audit noted that the inactive pane's dimming is subtle, so look closely to see which pane is active.
A fresh agent reviewed the branch at level high and found nothing in the code; the one skipped finding was this missing page.
CI's own review runs on the first push and reports in its code review comment.
CI's build, test run and review come on the first push, and its screenshots are audited after that.
Every test runs on the final head before the merge; the untested cases wait for daily use.
The PR, the issue, the branch, CI's comments and issue 128 are linked here.
lines.say: The PR, the issue, the branch, C I's comments and issue one twenty-eight are linked here.

lines.caption: Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 155.
lines.say: Part 3. Nothing depends on issue one fifty-five.

lines.caption: This PR builds on the tab lookup from issue 128, and no open issue builds on it yet.
lines.say: This PR builds on the tab lookup from issue one twenty-eight, and no open issue builds on it yet.

lines.caption: In short: Previous and Next Tab now treat both panes as one row of tabs, and follow you into the other pane.
lines.say: In short: Previous Tab and Next Tab now treat both panes as one row of tabs, and follow you into the other pane.
